messages.subject: predict.svcTMsPGOcc  crashing issue
parts:
Hi folks (specifically Jeff),

I am trying to model SGCN species distribution across Iowa. For prior context, I was having issues with computing power but found computers on campus that are relatively high-powered (48 cores, 128 GB RAM). I am working with some considerably large datasets and trying to predict 9101 sites (grid points spaced 4km apart) in Iowa using output from svcTMsPGOcc. For covariates, I am using the landscape metrics mean Euclidean distance and % in a 2km radius buffer for landcover types: developed, forest, grass, open water, and wetland for 10 covariates. I am currently running them all as SVCs just to see the output. Just as a note, we are working to finalize our covariate lists for each guild and which covariates will be run as SVCs. But for now, we assume all covariates are spatially varying across Iowa.

I have tried using occupancy outputs from 7 species grass bird guild (all with all but one species >1000 detections) and 5 species of Mustelid (all <200 detections) , both across 19 years. The issue I am running into is when I try to run the prediction, I make it all the way to the "generating latent occupancy state," and then the RStudio session aborts. I thought maybe it was still memory issues, so I then only took one year and only one "site" to predict onto (from Mustelids), and the issue is the same.

Has anyone had similar issues and figured it out?

Here is some of the basic code to set up models.
Occupancy Model
# Number of batches
n.batch <- 1000
# Batch length
batch.length <- 25
n.samples <- n.batch * batch.length
n.burn <- 1000
n.thin <- 20
n.factors <- 5
# Tuning
tuning.list <- list(phi = 1, rho = 1)

svc.cols <- c(1:11)


#Spatial occupancy SVC ----

out.svc = svcTMsPGOcc(
  occ.formula =  ~ #scale(Crop.enn_mn) + scale(Crop.pland) +
    scale(Developed.enn_mn) + scale(Developed.pland) +
    scale(Forest.enn_mn) + scale(Forest.pland) +
    scale(Grass.enn_mn) + scale(Grass.pland) +
    scale(Water.enn_mn) + scale(Water.pland) +
    scale(Wetlands.enn_mn) + scale(Wetlands.pland),
  svc.cols = svc.cols,
  det.formula = ~ scale(temp) + scale(day) + scale(wind),
  data = data.list,
  n.batch = n.batch,
  batch.length = batch.length,
  priors = prior.list,
  inits = inits.list,
  n.factors = n.factors,
  cov.model = "exponential",
  tuning = tuning.list,
  n.omp.threads = 40,
  NNGP = TRUE,
  ar1 = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  n.neighbors = 10,
  search.type = 'cb',
  n.report = 200,
  n.burn = n.burn,
  n.thin = n.thin,
  n.chains = 3
)


Predict model
out.pred = predict(
  out.svc,
  X.0,
  coords.0,
  n.omp.threads = 40,
  verbose = TRUE,
  t.cols = t.cols,
  ignore.RE = TRUE,
  n.report = 100,
  type = 'occupancy'
)

_____________________
Mic Rohde
PhD Student
NREM - Iowa State University

messages.subject: Re: predict.svcTMsPGOcc crashing issue
parts:
Hi Mic,

Unfortunately I don't have an answer for you, but I have been having a similar issue this week so I am keen to follow the discussion. I am predicting single-species spatial occupancy across Uganda with 8 covariates. I am lucky enough to have access to a computer with 48 GPUs and 1.2TB of RAM yet it still crashes when I get to the 'generating latent occupancy state' stage. I have tried reducing my resolution to 10km2 just to see if I can get it to run all the way through, but I've not had any luck predicting across the whole of Uganda yet. I have managed to get it to run on a tiny protected area (65km2) at a 1km resolution. I have also tried threading but it does not seem to work.

In case it's useful to help identify the issue, here is the original code I have been using:

cov.model <- "exponential" 
spat.tuning <- list(phi = 1)
spat.inits <- list(alpha = 0, 
                   beta = 0, 
                   z = apply(data$y, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE), 
                   sigma.sq = 2, 
                   w = rep(0, nrow(data$y)))
x2<-3/(56697.391/2)
w2<-1/528.7530110
informed.priors.ss <- list(beta.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72), 
                           alpha.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72), 
                           sigma.sq.ig = c(2, 1), 
                           phi.unif = c(x2, w2))

bay.mod9.1 <- spPGOcc(occ.formula = occ.9, 
                      det.formula = det.formula, 
                      data = data, 
                      inits = spat.inits,
                      n.batch = 4000,
                      batch.length = 25,
                      priors = informed.priors.ss,
                      cov.model = cov.model,
                      NNGP = TRUE,
                      n.neighbors = 15,
                      tuning = spat.tuning,
                      n.report = 1000, 
                      n.burn = 40000, 
                      n.thin = 20, 
                      n.chains = 3)

X.0<-as.matrix(stack1)
cent <- crds(as.points(stack1[[1]]))
gp.pred.9.1<-predict(bay.mod9.1, X.0, cent, type = "occupancy")


Many thanks in advance to anyone who might be able to recommend some solutions!

Thanks,
Naomi

messages.author: 0b274a0ee3490d75
messages.subject: Re: predict.svcTMsPGOcc crashing issue
parts:
Hi Mic and Naomi,

Thanks for the questions. The answers to your two questions are slightly different, so I'll respond one at a time:

Mic

This is interesting and I'm not exactly sure what is going on here just by looking at the code. First, as always, make sure you have the latest version installed from CRAN (0.8.0) because there's a chance this is related to a small memory problem I fixed a while back (although that is wishful thinking). The fact that you tested with only one year and one site and still got the error indicates to me there could be a bug in the underlying function. I don't think many folks have used this function before, so this could be something I haven't come upon yet. Would you be able to send me a reproducible example? I don't need the actual output from the spOccupancy run (e.g., the out.svc list), but if you can send the data in data.list and the data you were using for predictions so I can generate the error that would be super helpful for predicting. 

Also, as an aside, setting "n.omp.threads = 40" will actually likely slow the model down. The way the parallelization works, there is usually an optimum number of threads to set the values to that's usually around 10 or so, although it can vary depending on machine and data set. Regardless, I'd recommend bringing that down a bit to around 10 or so.

Naomi

When doing prediction over a large number of sites, the objects that the model needs to create are quite large (i.e., for spPGOcc a matrix with rows equal to the number of MCMC locations and columns equal to the number of sites). The way it's coded in spOccupancy requires these objects to be stored in continuous memory, which means that even if the object is not bigger than the amount of RAM on the computer, it may still run out of storage if it can't find enough continuous memory to store things. Long story short, the simplest way to get around this is to predict for a small amount of locations at a time, generate some summary output from those predictions, store those summaries in an array, and do this a bunch of times until you succeed for the whole prediction set. I talked a bit about this in a previous thread here. Try out that approach to see if that works, and if it doesn't then let me know. d

Jeff
